growth_012:n1.prompt:
You are helping me build the target contact list for an outbound sales sequence inside {{vendor}}, our CRM. Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already clear: (1) my {{vendor}} account access confirmation (use your configured credentials), (2) the ideal customer profile / targeting criteria (industry, company size, job titles, geography, etc.), (3) the source of prospects — e.g. a CSV/list I'll provide, a saved search, or criteria for you to search against enriched data, and (4) any custom fields I want tracked (e.g. sequence name, lead source, priority tier).

Once you have this, do the following in {{vendor}}:
1. Create the target contact records (and linked company records where applicable) via the CRM's API or dashboard, matching the ICP criteria I gave you.
2. Ensure each contact/company record is enriched with available firmographic and contact data (title, company size, industry, etc.) — either automatically or by triggering the enrichment feature.
3. Add any custom fields I requested to the contact records.
4. Build a filtered, sorted view of this new target list and share it (or confirm it's shared) so it's usable by the team, not just saved privately.
5. Verify each contact has a proper activity timeline started (even if empty) so replies and calls can be logged later.

Done looks like: a clean, de-duplicated list of target contacts (with linked companies) sitting in {{vendor}}, enriched with firmographic data, tagged with any custom fields, and visible in a named, filtered/shared view ready to be pulled into a sequence.

Report back with: the number of contacts created, the name/link of the saved view, a summary of enrichment coverage (e.g. % with title/company data filled), and any records that failed to create or enrich so I can review them.

growth_012:n2.prompt:
You are helping me draft outbound sales sequence copy inside {{vendor}}, our CRM. Before starting, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available in the CRM or my notes: our ideal customer profile / target list criteria, the product or service being sold, our value proposition and key differentiators, 2-3 customer proof points or case studies, the desired sequence length (e.g., number of steps and channels - email, LinkedIn, call tasks), and my preferred tone (formal, casual, direct).

Once you have the inputs, do the following inside {{vendor}}:
1. Use the product's built-in AI assistant to generate a first draft of a multi-step outbound sequence (typically 4-6 touches) tailored to the target segment, referencing our value proposition and proof points.
2. Pull any AI-generated insights or suggestions the CRM offers on messaging, subject lines, or send timing based on our historical data, and incorporate the useful ones into the draft.
3. Write clear, concise copy for each step: subject lines, email body, and any LinkedIn or call-task scripts, with a single clear call-to-action per step (usually booking a meeting).
4. Personalize with merge fields/tokens supported by the CRM's templating (name, company, role, etc.).
5. Save the sequence as a draft template inside the CRM, organized under a clearly labeled sequence name so it's easy to find later.
6. Do not launch or activate the sequence yet — that is a separate step.

When done, report back to me with: the sequence name/location in {{vendor}}, the number of steps and channels used, a summary of the AI-generated suggestions you incorporated, and the full copy for each step so I can review it. Flag anything you're unsure about (tone, claims, compliance language) so I can confirm before launch.

growth_012:n3.prompt:
You are helping me set up an outbound email sequence in {{vendor}}, our CRM, but you must NOT launch it until I explicitly approve. If you don't already have these from me, ask for: (1) the {{vendor}} workspace/domain details, (2) the target list criteria or the list of prospects already loaded in the CRM, (3) the sequence goal (e.g. book a demo), (4) the number of steps and cadence (e.g. 4 emails over 10 days, with any follow-up call/task steps), and (5) tone/positioning notes for the emails.

Using your configured credentials, do the following inside {{vendor}}: draft the multi-step email sequence with subject lines and body copy for each touch, using merge fields for personalization (name, company, etc.). Configure any trigger-based rules needed — e.g., auto-advance to the next step if no reply, stop the sequence and create a task for me when a prospect replies, and notify me when a meeting-worthy reply comes in. If the target list isn't fully built, prepare the list criteria and segment definition for review. Save everything as a draft/inactive sequence — do not enroll prospects or send anything yet.

When ready, give me a summary report: the sequence name, number of steps and cadence, a copy of each email draft, the trigger rules configured, the target list size and criteria, and any settings I need to confirm (e.g. sending domain, throttling limits). Then stop for human sign-off — I will review and give explicit approval before you activate the sequence or enroll any prospects.

growth_012:n4.prompt:
You are helping me operate the outbound sales sequence I've already built in {{vendor}}. This step covers sending the sequence and monitoring replies as they arrive over the following days — this is an async step, so you'll need to poll or verify status rather than expect instant results.

First, ask me for anything you need that's missing: my {{vendor}} instance details, the name of the sequence/campaign to launch, confirmation that my Gmail or Outlook mailbox is already connected for two-way sync, and whether webhook or notification subscriptions for reply-related events are already configured (if not, ask if you should set up a webhook subscription for reply and bounce events using your configured credentials).

Then: (1) Confirm the target contact/company list is loaded and linked to the sequence. (2) Launch or resume the sequence send inside {{vendor}}, describing the action in words (e.g. 'start the sequence' via the dashboard or API) — do not invent specific endpoint calls. (3) Set up or verify a way to monitor replies — via webhook events if available, or by periodically checking each contact's activity timeline in {{vendor}} for new inbound emails, out-of-office replies, or bounces. (4) For each new reply detected, log a summary (contact name, company, reply content snippet, sentiment — interested/not interested/needs follow-up) and flag any that look meeting-ready.

Done looks like: the sequence is actively sending, a monitoring mechanism (webhook or polling cadence) is confirmed working, and you can produce a running list of new replies with status tags as they come in.

Report back with: confirmation the sequence launched, how monitoring is set up (webhook vs. polling and frequency), and a running log/table of replies received so far with contact, snippet, and suggested next action (e.g. 'route to book meeting').

growth_012:n5.prompt:
You are helping me book meetings with prospects who replied positively to my outbound sales sequence, using {{vendor}} (my scheduling tool) connected to my CRM.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already configured:
- Which CRM/inbox holds the list of responders (e.g., replies marked 'interested' or 'meeting requested')
- My {{vendor}} event type slug/username to use for these bookings
- Any team round-robin or priority routing rules if multiple reps should receive these meetings
- Confirmation that {{vendor}} is already connected with my configured credentials (via API or MCP tool-calling)

Then do the following:
1. Pull the list of responders who need a meeting booked (from CRM records or reply threads I point you to).
2. For each responder, check available times using {{vendor}} and either create a booking directly (using the event type and responder's email/name) or generate a personalized booking link for them to pick a time themselves — use whichever approach I prefer.
3. If a responder later asks to change time, reschedule the existing booking rather than creating a duplicate.
4. Ensure each booking syncs into the CRM record for that responder (contact/deal updated with meeting time and status) — if this isn't automatic, flag it so I can wire up the integration.
5. If multiple reps are involved, apply the round-robin/priority rule I gave you when assigning meetings.
6. Keep a running log of: responder name, meeting time booked, event type used, and CRM record link.

Done looks like: every responder on the list either has a confirmed meeting on the calendar or a booking link sent to them, all bookings reflected in the CRM, and no duplicate/conflicting meetings.

Report back with a summary table of responders processed, meetings booked vs. links sent, any reschedules, and any responders you couldn't process (with the reason) so I can follow up manually.

growth_012:n6.prompt:
You are helping me prepare for qualification calls that come out of my outbound sales sequence. The actual live call — reading tone, handling objections, and building rapport with the prospect — remains a human step that you cannot perform. Your job is to prepare everything I need so I can run the conversation myself.

Please ask me for anything missing: my target ICP/qualification criteria (e.g., BANT, MEDDIC, or a custom framework), my CRM (e.g., HubSpot, Salesforce, Pipedrive), and the list of upcoming booked meetings or replies awaiting a call, plus any context notes on those prospects already in the CRM.

Then do the following:
1. Pull together a one-page qualification call brief for each upcoming call: prospect name, company, role, how they entered the sequence, any reply/email context, and known firmographic details.
2. Draft a qualification call script or talk-track template tailored to my stated framework, including opening rapport lines, 5-8 discovery questions, common objection responses, and a closing ask (next step/meeting).
3. Create a structured notes template (fields matching my qualification framework) that I can fill in live during or right after each call.
4. Prepare a checklist of pre-call prep items (review CRM history, confirm meeting time/timezone, check company news) for each scheduled call.
5. Draft a placeholder CRM update format (fields to fill: qualified/disqualified, next step, notes) so I can log outcomes quickly after each call.

Done looks like: for every upcoming call I have a brief, a talk-track, a notes template, and a prep checklist ready, plus a standard format for logging the outcome in the CRM. Do not attempt to join, simulate, or conduct any live call yourself — stop for human sign-off before I run each call, and report back a summary of what's prepared and any prospects missing enough context for you to build a proper brief.
